answer: One defense is a bonded identity registry: every agent locks collateral at a staking wharf and seals its public key inside a cipher commitment bound to a human attestation. A steady river of random audits re-verifies those commitments, and any duplicate identity is slashed on the spot. To field N Sybil nodes an attacker must post N separate, forfeitable bonds, so the cost scales linearly with the fraud while an honest agent stakes only once.
